candidates.locator: Page 8 of PART IV, part_i (preceding Section 4)
candidates.exact_span: The annual whole sludge application rate for the sewage sludge that does not cause any of the cumulative pollutant loading rates in Table 2 above to be exceeded, unless the pollutant concentrations in Table 3 found in Element I, Section III below are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties enforceable numeric compliance to either cumulative pollutant loading rates (Table 2) or an alternative pathway when Table 3 concentration criteria are met. Different readings of which branch applies, or how the annual whole sludge application rate interacts with those limits, could change which numeric limit is selected for comparison (Purpose A) and how missing or conditional sludge data should be classified when the Table 3 exception may apply (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 3 found in Element I, Section III and the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/Kg), or the applicable cumulative pollutant loading rate and the applicable cumulative pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause specifies the numeric pollutant concentration criteria and cumulative loading-rate limits that must be recorded. Interpretation of whether concentration criteria or cumulative loading limits govern a given pollutant/site affects which enforceable numeric limit applies (Purpose A), whether developing and retaining this information is an applicable obligation (Purpose B), and whether absent records reflect documented no-data, unmet recordkeeping obligations, or unresolved evidence (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The person who prepares bulk sewage sludge or a sewage sludge material shall develop the following information and shall retain the information for five years.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The five-year retention duty defines how long sludge concentration and loading evidence should exist. Different interpretation of who qualifies as the preparer, or whether FY2025 falls within the retention window, could change whether recordkeeping/monitoring obligations were applicable during the fiscal year (Purpose B) and whether missing sludge data is adequately explained or remains unresolved (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: If the permittee supplies the sludge to another person who land applies the sludge, the permittee shall notify the land applier of the requirements for recordkeeping found in 40 CFR 503.17 for persons who land apply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This shifts recordkeeping obligations to land appliers via cross-reference to 40 CFR 503.17. Whether the permittee or the land applier bears the operative recordkeeping duty affects which monitoring/recordkeeping requirements were applicable for FY2025 (Purpose B) and whose missing records constitute inadequate evidence versus an unresolved allocation of responsibility (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall give 60 days prior notice to the Director of any change planned in the sewage sludge practice. Any change shall include any planned physical alterations or additions to the permitted treatment works, changes in the permittee's sludge use or disposal practice, and also alterations, additions, or deletions of disposal sites. These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit, including notification of additional disposal sites not reported during the permit application process or absent in the existing permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Changes in sludge use, disposal sites, or treatment works during FY2025 may trigger different permit conditions. Interpretation of what counts as a covered change, and whether revised conditions were in effect during a given period, could change which monitoring or notification requirements were actually applicable in that period (Purpose B).
